script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. Thursday — here is your QQQ recap. The portfolio closed up six point four eight percent on the session. It was a broad-based rally, and several positions moved in a way that demands your full attention right now.

Micron Technology surged eighteen point three six percent on Thursday. That is not a rounding error. Multi-year automotive AI supply agreements, now materializing into market conviction, sent the stock to one of its strongest single-session moves in recent memory.

The broad market staged a sharp recovery Thursday, led by technology and semiconductor names after Microsoft's earnings results triggered a wave of buying across the artificial intelligence supply chain. At least one headline noted United States equity indexes surging as inflation data for June came in favorably, providing additional fuel for the move.

Microsoft delivered the catalyst that reset the tone for the entire session. The company reported second-quarter results that drove the stock up fifteen point five one percent — a move of that magnitude, on a position that size, is consequential for this portfolio. The cloud computing division led the quarter, and analysts pointed to accelerating enterprise adoption of artificial intelligence services as the primary driver. The earnings call framed artificial intelligence infrastructure spending not as an experiment but as a committed, multi-year capital cycle. For holders, Microsoft's result was a read-through signal for nearly every other position in the portfolio — from memory to chips to hyperscale infrastructure — and Thursday's price action across the book reflected exactly that.

Nvidia was up two point six five percent on the session. The direct news was centered on Super Micro Computer's announcement of a new rack series engineered specifically for high-density artificial intelligence data center deployments, with configurations certified for load capacities exceeding five thousand five hundred pounds and optimized for liquid cooling. Supermicro is a key infrastructure partner in the Nvidia ecosystem, and expanded rack deployment capacity speaks directly to continued demand pull for Nvidia's compute hardware. Watch for any updated data center spending commentary from hyperscale customers in the days ahead.

Apple was down one point four one percent on the session, and that decline extended into after-hours following earnings. Revenue rose sixteen percent to one hundred nine point four billion dollars, and earnings per share climbed twenty-nine percent — both ahead of estimates. But services revenue missed expectations, and analysts flagged rising memory costs as a potential headwind to iPhone pricing going forward. The stock sold off on the miss in a high-margin business line. Services is the growth engine Wall Street values most. That is the number to watch in subsequent quarters.

Alphabet was down zero point nine one percent on the session, though the company's cloud computing business drew bullish commentary, with one piece noting what it called five hundred fourteen billion reasons to revisit the shares — a reference to cloud-driven earnings momentum. Turning to Micron Technology — up eighteen point three six percent, as covered in the top story. The automotive artificial intelligence supply agreements signed with Qualcomm, Visteon, HARMAN, DENSO, and Hyundai Mobis are providing long-term revenue visibility that the market is now pricing in aggressively.

Amazon was up three point nine zero percent. Cloud growth at Amazon Web Services accelerated to a more than four-year high, with the division growing thirty-seven percent to forty-two point four billion dollars. After-hours, the stock diverged from Apple, moving higher on earnings momentum. Advanced Micro Devices was up thirteen point zero zero percent — a direct beneficiary of the Microsoft-driven artificial intelligence infrastructure rally, with semiconductor names broadly repriced higher. Intel was up eleven point three zero percent on the session. No specific news drove the move, but Intel's gains were consistent with the broad semiconductor rebound that swept the sector Thursday on the back of Microsoft's results and favorable macro data. Watch for any follow-through in chip equipment names. Tesla was up three point five three percent on the session, participating in the broader risk-on move. A bearish forecast circulating Thursday suggested Tesla could lose its trillion-dollar market capitalization before the end of twenty twenty-six, citing a price level approximately sixteen percent below current trading. That is a thesis worth monitoring.

Over at Lam Research — a secondary holding — up seventeen point nine eight percent. Applied Materials up fourteen point nine seven percent. Sandisk up twenty-five point nine nine percent. The semiconductor equipment and memory storage complex moved in lockstep with the broader chip rally. These secondary positions amplified the portfolio's Thursday performance meaningfully.

Three data points to track in the next forty-eight hours. First, any analyst revisions following Apple's earnings miss in services — that segment repricing will matter for the stock's near-term direction. Second, Advanced Micro Devices reports earnings imminently — given Thursday's thirteen percent move, the market is already pricing in strength, raising the bar for the actual print. Third, watch Federal Reserve speakers for any commentary on the June inflation data referenced Thursday — rate expectations remain a ceiling or floor for technology valuations broadly.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. With Microsoft's print now in the books and Advanced Micro Devices earnings on deck, Friday's session will tell us whether Thursday's artificial intelligence rally has legs or was a single-session reaction.
